newsitem.title: IRAQ: Oil deal shows U.S. influence decline - Iraq papers.
newsitem.headline: Oil deal shows U.S. influence decline - Iraq papers.

text.p: Official Iraqi newspapers said on Tuesday Baghdad's agreement to U.N. terms for for the flow of partial Iraqi oil exports indicated that Washington's influence in the world body was on the wane.

The agreement over terms of implementing an oil-for-food deal, announced in New York on Monday by Iraq's U.N. ambassador Nizar Hamdoon, "came at a very suitable time for Iraq", the government newspaper al-Jumhouriya said.

It said the agreement marked "a turning point in the balance of power inside the (U.N.) Security Council and the imposition of sometimes severe restrictions on the freedom of America in issuing decisions and passing resolutions."
"The agreement is important because it removes the excuses on which the United States and with it Britain relied to hamper the implementation of the memorandum of understanding," the paper said.
Babel, the newspaper of President Saddam Hussein eldest Uday, said the imminent flow of Iraqi oil showed how "impotent" Washington was in confronting Iraq.

The oil-for-food deal, signed by Iraq and the United Nations in May, is designed to help ease the effects on Iraqis of crippling economic sanctions imposed soon after Iraq invaded Kuwait in August 1990.
It allows Baghdad to export $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy food and medicine under strict U.N. supervision.

Baghdad had previously accused Washington of delaying the implementation of the oil-for-food deal. The pact was put on hold when Baghdad sent troops into northern Iraq late in August in support of one Kurdish faction against another.
The Baghdad papers splashed their front-pages with reports on Iraq's readiness to export oil once it gets the green light from the United Nations.
The partial oil sales could amount to about 700,000-800,00 barrels per day (bpd) at current prices. Before the U.N. sanctions Iraq exported more than 2.5 million bpd.
Hamdoon predicted Iraqi oil exports would start in December.
An end to the overall curbs on oil exports depends on Iraq coming clean about its fromer biological, chemical and nuclear weapons programmes.
News of Iraq's agreement to the U.N. terms immediately strengthened the value of the Iraqi dinar on Monday to 1,100 to the dollar from 1,650.
